title: Pulse Canary: safety checklist and ops journal (working)
body:
Purpose:
Short working notes for a lightweight 'pulse' canary pattern: repeated very small exposures of a new model or config to detect fast regressions without allocating large traffic slices. Idea: punctuated micro-samples + automated evaluation hooks to catch behavioral drift (latency, hallucination, safety triggers, cost spikes) within minutes.

Pulse characteristics:
- Duration: 30s–3m per pulse (tunable).
- Frequency: every 15m–2h depending on risk profile.
- Traffic slice: 0.05%–0.5% of live traffic or fixed request cap (e.g., 200 reqs/pulse).
- Synthetic probe set: 30 canonical prompts (language/length/edge-case mix) run in parallel with live samples.

Pre-flight checklist (must be green before first pulse):
1) Baseline collected: last-stable model metrics (p50/p95 latency, error rate, safety triggers, cost_per_request).
2) Probe set validated: golden outputs and auto-eval scripts committed to repo.
3) Fallback configured: automatic reroute to stable model + rate-limiter on retries.
4) Rollback playbook: Slack channel, oncall contact, quick rollback runbook exists.
5) Observability: dashboards with p50/p95, token counts, safety-classifier rate, hallucination proxy, model error codes.
6) Guardrail policy: max allowed delta thresholds set (see thresholds section).

Immediate rollback thresholds (example heuristics):
- Latency: p95 increases by more than 50% vs baseline for 2 consecutive pulses.
- Errors: user-facing error rate (4xx/5xx or internal failures) > 1.5% absolute and 100% relative increase vs baseline.
- Safety: safety-classifier triggers up > 3x or +0.5% absolute for two pulses.
- Quality (auto-eval): hallucination rate on probe set increases by >5 percentage points.
- Cost: average tokens/request jumps >40% or unexpected token distribution.
Note: thresholds should be conservative for high-risk cohorts and permissive for low-risk internal experiments.

Triage flow (fast path):
1) Confirm signal: correlate metrics across dashboards and probe results.
2) Instrumentation check: ensure no ingestion lag, no missing telemetry, check agent health.
3) Reproduce: run the synthetic probe set directly against the canary and the baseline side-by-side.
4) Narrow: if signal isolated to a route/model variant, pause that slice; otherwise pause all pulses.
5) Rollback: divert routing to stable model and run a smoke-check on a few live requests.
6) Post-mortem: capture findings in this ops journal and open follow-up tickets (root cause, mitigation, monitoring gaps).

Notification templates (quick):
- Slack alert (canary-failure): "Pulse Canary {canary_id} -> observed p95↑ {value}% and safety triggers↑ {value}. Pausing pulses and diverting traffic to {stable_model}. Oncall: @{name}. Triage in progress."
- Pager (SEV): "Pulse Canary auto-rollback triggered for {canary_id} due to {primary_signal}. See {link-to-dashboard}."

Sample telemetry queries (promQL-like pseudo):
- p95 latency by model: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{model=~"canary|stable"}[5m])) by (le, model))
- safety classifier count: sum(rate(safety_trigger_total{model="canary"}[5m]))
- probe-set hallucination regression: rate(auto_eval_hallucination{probe_set="pulse30",model="canary"}[5m]) - rate(auto_eval_hallucination{probe_set="pulse30",model="baseline"}[5m])

Ops journal template (append one entry per pulse/event):
- date: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ
- canary_id: pulse-YYYYMMDD-HHMM
- model: model-name@sha
- traffic: percent/cap/route
- duration: seconds
- probe-results: PASS/FAIL + key diffs (latency, hallucination %)
- live-signals: p50/p95/cost_per_request/safety_triggers/error_rate
- actions: pause|continue|rollback|escalate + who
- notes: freeform observations, reproducible examples, next steps

Recent journal example (mock):
- 2025-02-10T11:15Z | pulse-20250210-1115 | model: targa-3b@sha1234 | 0.2% traffic cap 250reqs | duration 120s | probe: halluc +1.2pp, p95 +22% | live: safety triggers +0.4% | action: paused, rerouted to stable, opened JIRA-PLAT-1142 | notes: signal marginal; root cause likely tokenization variant with longer system prompts

Open questions / next steps:
- Can we automate confidence-weighted rollback (combine signals into a single score)?
- Should we gate pulse frequency by business-critical routes only?
- Add synthetic negative prompts that historically surface hallucinations for regression sensitivity.
- Bake a small internal simulator to estimate time-to-detect for different pulse configs.

If you use this template: leave a short note in the journal each time you run a pulse (even if nothing happened). Small repeated entries are the best signal for drift over time.

---
Notes to self: integrate with rollout-console demo flow; coordinate with SRE on throttling and with safety team to tune classifier thresholds before expanding beyond internal cohorts.
